summary: Dispatched the decoupling case the last discriminator called for, after a local run that already changes the reading. The harness now takes the follower's flush deadline as a parameter (every earlier case used the fixed hundred ticks), and the new case keeps the tick period at 1000 ms — where the shift was reproduced three times — while reducing that deadline to two ticks. Locally the fresh call then returned index 4 with entry 33 actually at index 4 (`assigned_idx_matches_true_index` true), the decided values were 11,12,22,33,34,35 and `decided_after_resync` was 3, so the origin's earlier buffered entries survived instead of being discarded. The shift therefore does not follow from the tick period alone: with a fast follower flush at the same tick period it did not occur, which is what the source trace of the flush deferral implied. That narrows the account without contradicting the violation, which remains reproduced under the original configuration; I submitted the case so the decoupling rests on a receipt and left the corrected interpretation and knowledge revision for the next update, since the evidence for them exists only once this receipt does. Incomplete: which of the two factors is necessary remains open, and a run varying only the tick period at a fast flush (or a slow flush at a small tick) would settle it.
